titulo: Your first loop: a small goal with a level 3 criterion
lead: Time to put the pieces together in a real loop, small on purpose: a word-counting function, six tests frozen with a hash, and a level 3 /goal condition with a turn cap. Small enough to finish in minutes; complete enough to have all five pieces. At the end, the map of the track and your plan with dates.
objetivo: run your first loop with /goal on a small project, with frozen tests, a level 3 criterion, and a turn cap, and leave with the track plan.

secoes.titulo: The project for your first loop
secoes.sub: One folder, one test file frozen by hash, and not a single line of the function. The agent writes the function.

blocos.rot: Terminal · create the folder and freeze the tests
blocos.conteudo:
mkdir -p ~/ensaio-loop/conta/tests && cd ~/ensaio-loop/conta && git init -q
# paste the test file from the next block into tests/test_conta.py, then:
sha256sum tests/test_conta.py > tests.sha256
git add -A && git commit -qm "testes congelados"
python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/ | tail -1   # still fails: conta.py does not exist

blocos.rot: Claude Code · the /goal condition (level 3, with a cap)
blocos.conteudo: /goal python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/ prints 6 passed, sha256sum -c tests.sha256 prints OK and git diff --exit-code -- tests/ exits with code 0, with all three outputs printed in the conversation, or stop after 8 turns

blocos.rot: Terminal · you check it, without trusting the summary
blocos.conteudo:
cd ~/ensaio-loop/conta
python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/ | tail -1
sha256sum -c tests.sha256
git diff --exit-code -- tests/; echo "rc=$?"

blocos.rot: loop-codex.sh · the same loop with codex exec (exercise 3)
blocos.conteudo:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Your own loop: at most 3 cycles of codex exec; the three commands decide when to stop.
set -u
cd ~/ensaio-loop/conta
passes() {
  python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/ 2>&1 | tail -1 | grep -q '^6 passed' &&
  sha256sum -c --quiet tests.sha256 &&
  git diff --quiet -- tests/
}
for ciclo in 1 2 3; do
  if passes; then echo "PRONTO no ciclo $((ciclo - 1))"; exit 0; fi
  echo "ciclo $ciclo: codex exec"
  timeout 15m codex exec --sandbox workspace-write \
    "Crie conta.py com conta_palavras(texto) que faça os testes de tests/ passarem. Não altere nada em tests/."
done
if passes; then echo "PRONTO no ciclo 3"; exit 0; fi
echo "PARADO: teto de 3 ciclos"; exit 2

abas.html:
With the same condition, in headless mode (claude -p "/goal …"), the agent wrote conta.py and finished by printing:

- python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/ → 6 passed in 0.01s
- sha256sum -c tests.sha256 → tests/test_conta.py: OK
- git diff --exit-code -- tests/ → saiu com código 0

Its function and yours may be different; what has to match are the three outputs.

$ echo "def test_x(): pass" > tests/test_conta.py
$ sha256sum -c tests.sha256
tests/test_conta.py: FAILED
sha256sum: WARNING: 1 computed checksum did NOT match
$ echo $?
1

Swapping the test for an empty one would make pytest pass, but the hash and the git diff flag it. That's the difference between level 2 and level 3.

• Objective: the /goal condition.
  • State: the files and the tests commit.
  • Action: the agent editing conta.py.
  • Verification: pytest with a count, hash and git diff, printed in the conversation.
  • Stop: the /goal evaluator or the 8-turn cap.

secoes.sub: On your machine. Exercise 2 uses little of your quota.

exercicios.titulo: E1 · The project ready for the loop
exercicios.texto: Create the folder, the test file, the hash and the first commit. Run pytest before the function exists.
exercicios.pronto: sha256sum -c tests.sha256 → tests/test_conta.py: OK, git log --oneline | wc -l → 1, and pytest still fails (the function doesn't exist).

exercicios.texto: Open Claude Code in the folder and paste the /goal condition. Let it run without interfering; if Claude asks permission to run pytest, approve it.
exercicios.pronto: The goal status shows the condition met, and the three check commands, run by you, give 6 passed, tests/test_conta.py: OK and rc=0.

exercicios.titulo: E3 · The same loop with Codex
exercicios.texto: Delete conta.py and run the same request through codex exec with a write sandbox, using the loop-codex.sh from the block above: at most 3 cycles, stopping when the three commands pass.
exercicios.pronto: Your loop ends before the 3rd cycle, and the same three commands give 6 passed, OK and rc=0; git diff --stat -- tests/ comes out empty.

txt.titulo: Plan — Base: anatomy of the loop
txt.travou: ## What got stuck and the rule I created

perguntas.p: Why does the /goal condition ask for "all three outputs printed in the conversation"?
opcoes: Because the /goal evaluator only reads the conversation: without the printed output, it judges by the agent's word
Because pytest doesn't print anything on its own
perguntas.explica: It's question 4 on the scale: does the proof show up in the output? The evaluator doesn't run the commands; the agent does, and the output has to be there to be judged.

perguntas.p: What does the hash in tests.sha256 add to "6 passed"?
opcoes: Proof that the test file is the same one you froze, closing the shortcut of rewriting the tests
perguntas.explica: "6 passed" alone is level 2: an agent can swap the tests for six others that pass. The hash and the git diff lock the file. Together, level 3.

perguntas.p: The /goal finished with the condition met. What's the next step?
opcoes: Run the three check commands yourself
Ask the agent to check again
perguntas.explica: You close it: the evaluator judged the conversation, you check the machine. It's what the execucao-longa kit asks for at the close of every run.

perguntas.p: After this course, what's next in the suggested order of the track?
perguntas.explica: The suggested order is 0 → 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5. Course 1 takes the piece that's missing most, verification, and brings it up to level 4.

itens.texto: The first loop has all five pieces on a problem that finishes in minutes.
Tests with a hash and a commit before the agent starts: that's what makes the criterion level 3.
The evaluator judges the conversation; you run the check on the machine.
